verdict.rationale: Cline is a coding agent that is operated through natural-language conversation. The docs say it can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser and build features "through natural conversation". CLI examples accept plain-English commands such as "run tests and fix failures" and "review these changes", and community users report daily-driving it this way. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration covers the editor and terminal workflow only, not the chat channels (Slack/Discord) or headless natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: It can read and write files, run terminal commands, use a browser, and help you build features through natural conversation.
cline --auto-approve true "run tests and fix failures"
Chat with the agent from Slack, Discord, Telegram, or Linear.
I can plan with it for 10-15 minutes, set it loose on my codebase, go get lunch, and then its diff is almost always completely on the money.
